node.title: Regex bug? matching multiple newline with /m
node.author: NERDVANA
node.doctext:
Hi, I ran across a strange behavior and I'm wondering if it is a bug, or some obscure documented behavior I should keep in mind.

These match: # (not using 'say' because I wanted to try it on old perl versions) perl -e 'printf "%s ", "ab ab " =~ /^ab$ab$/m' perl -e 'printf "%s ", "ab ab " =~ /^(ab$ab$)/m' perl -e 'printf "%s ", "ab ab " =~ /^(ab$ab)$/m' perl -e 'printf "%s ", "ab ab " =~ /^(ab)$ab$/m' perl -e 'printf "%s ", "ab ab " =~ /^(a)b$ab$/m'

(with '$' consuming a " " because it is /m mode)

These do not match: perl -e 'printf "%s ", "ab ab " =~ /^(ab$a)b$/m' perl -e 'printf "%s ", "ab ab " =~ /^(ab$)ab$/m' perl -e 'printf "%s ", "ab ab " =~ /^ab$(ab)$/m' perl -e 'printf "%s ", "ab ab " =~ /^(ab$){2}/m' perl -e 'printf "%s ", "ab ab " =~ /(ab$){2}/m' perl -e 'printf "%s ", "ab ab " =~ /(?^:^(?^m:(ab$){2}))/m'

This is greedy but only matches one line perl -e 'printf "%s ", "ab ab " =~ /^((?:ab$)+)/m'

and it seems to me that all of them should match. This appears to happen as old as 5.8.9 and as new as 5.32.1

Any insights?
